source.text: Περὶ δὲ τῶν χρόνων καὶ τῶν καιρῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ὑμῖν γράφεσθαι, αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκριβῶς οἴδατε ὅτι ἡμέρα κυρίου ὡς κλέπτης ἐν νυκτὶ οὕτως ἔρχεται.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning now the times and the seasons, brothers, no need you have to you to be written, \v 2 yourselves for accurately you know that [the] day of [the] Lord as a thief in [the] night so comes.

en.L: Now concerning the times and the seasons, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you have no need for anything to be written to you, \v 2 for you yourselves know accurately that [the] day of [the] Lord comes like a thief in [the] night.
en.B: As for times and dates, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, there is no need for us to write to you. \v 2 You know very well yourselves that the Lord's day comes like a thief at night.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we do not need to write to you about when these things will happen. \v 2 You already know that the day when the Lord comes back will be a surprise, like a thief who comes at night.

decisions.choice: the times and the seasons: when the end will come
decisions.reason: The pair is a set phrase for the times God has fixed (Daniel 2:21; Acts 1:7, where Jesus says it is not for his followers to know them).

decisions.choice: the day of the Lord: the day of God's judgment and rescue, now the day of Christ's coming
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "the day of the LORD" (Amos 5:18-20; Joel 2:31). For Paul the Lord of that day is Jesus (4:15-17).

decisions.choice: like a thief in the night: without warning
decisions.reason: Jesus used the same picture (Matthew 24:43; Luke 12:39). The point is not that the day is evil but that it comes unannounced. The present ἔρχεται speaks of a sure fact.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: when these things will happen; will be a surprise
alternatives: the times and the seasons; like a thief in the night
decisions.reason: Readable says what "times and seasons" means and what the picture of the thief points to (m1, m3).

source.text: ὅταν λέγωσιν· Εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια, τότε αἰφνίδιος αὐτοῖς ἐφίσταται ὄλεθρος ὥσπερ ἡ ὠδὶν τῇ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκφύγωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: When they say, "Peace and security," then sudden upon them comes destruction, as the labor pain to the [woman] in womb having, and by no means will they escape.

en.L: When they are saying, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction comes upon them, like labor pains on a woman who is pregnant, and they will by no means escape.
en.B: Just when people are saying, "All is peaceful and safe," ruin will fall on them without warning, as labor pains come on a woman who is expecting a child, and there will be no escape.
en.R: People will be saying, "Everything is peaceful and safe." Then, suddenly, they will be destroyed. It will come on them like the pains of a woman who is about to give birth, and they will not be able to escape.

decisions.choice: "Peace and security": a false confidence
decisions.reason: The words echo the false prophets of Jeremiah 6:14 who said "Peace, peace" when there was no peace. "Peace and security" was also a theme of Roman claims about the empire, and the readers may have heard it that way; that echo is possible rather than certain.

decisions.choice: like labor pains: sudden, certain and inescapable
decisions.reason: The prophets compared the coming of God's judgment to a woman's labor (Isaiah 13:8; Jeremiah 6:24): it comes at a time no one can choose, and once it starts it cannot be stopped.

decisions.choice: destruction: ruin
decisions.reason: ὄλεθρος is ruin or destruction, the opposite of the "salvation" of verse 9.

decisions.choice: "All is peaceful and safe" (B); "Everything is peaceful and safe" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the slogan as people would say it; Literal keeps "Peace and security".

source.text: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σκότει, ἵνα ἡ ἡμέρα ὑμᾶς ὡς κλέπτης καταλάβῃ, πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς υἱοὶ φωτός ἐστε καὶ υἱοὶ ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: You but, brothers, not are in darkness, so that the day you like a thief should overtake, \v 5 all for you sons of light are and sons of day.

en.L: But you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, are not in darkness, so that the day would overtake you like a thief, \v 5 for you are all {{gender:children|sons}} of light and {{gender:children|sons}} of [the] day.
en.B: But you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, are not living in darkness, for that day to catch you by surprise like a thief. \v 5 You are all {{gender:children|sons}} of light and {{gender:children|sons}} of the day.
en.R: But {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you are not living in darkness, so that day will not take you by surprise like a thief. \v 5 All of you belong to the light and to the day.

decisions.choice: in darkness: in ignorance and wrongdoing, cut off from God
decisions.reason: Darkness is the realm of those who do not know God (Colossians 1:13). Believers live in the light, so the day will not find them unprepared.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "like a thief"
alternatives: "like thieves" (the day would overtake you as daylight catches thieves)
decisions.reason: A few important manuscripts read "thieves", which would picture the day catching them like thieves surprised by the dawn. The SBLGNT reads the singular, which matches verse 2.

decisions.choice: sons of light, sons of day: people who belong to the light
decisions.reason: "Sons of" something is a Hebrew way of saying people marked by it (compare "sons of disobedience", Colossians 3:6). It includes all believers, men and women.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means all believers (m3); "sons" is the traditional form. Readable says "belong to", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: All of you belong to the light and to the day
alternatives: you are all sons of light and sons of day
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m3).

source.text: οὐκ ἐσμὲν νυκτὸς οὐδὲ σκότους·

records.literal_gloss: Not we are of night nor of darkness;

en.L: We are not of [the] night or of darkness.
en.B: We do not belong to the night or to darkness.
en.R: We do not belong to the night or to the darkness.

decisions.choice: we: Paul includes himself with them
decisions.reason: ἐσμὲν ("we are") moves from "you" to "we": Paul speaks as one of them, and the exhortations that follow say "let us".

source.text: ἄρα οὖν μὴ καθεύδωμεν ὡς οἱ λοιποί, ἀλλὰ γρηγορῶμεν καὶ νήφωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: So then not let us sleep as the rest, but let us keep awake and let us be sober.

en.L: So then let us not sleep as the rest [do], but let us keep awake and be sober.
en.B: So then, we must not sleep like the rest, but stay awake and keep a clear head.
en.R: So we must not be like other people, who are asleep. We must stay awake and keep our minds clear.

decisions.choice: sleep: spiritual dullness, not death
decisions.reason: Here the verb is καθεύδωμεν, set against keeping awake: it means careless indifference, as in Mark 13:35-37. In 4:13-15 a different verb is used for those who have died. In verse 10 the same verb as here returns, but there it most likely means death.

decisions.choice: keep awake and be sober: alert and clear-headed
decisions.reason: γρηγορέω is to stay awake and watch (Mark 14:38); νήφω is to be sober, self-controlled (1 Peter 5:8).

decisions.choice: keep a clear head (B); keep our minds clear (R)
decisions.reason: "Sober" today mostly means not drunk; here it means clear-minded and self-controlled (m2).

source.text: οἱ γὰρ καθεύδοντες νυκτὸς καθεύδουσιν, καὶ οἱ μεθυσκόμενοι νυκτὸς μεθύουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: The [ones] for sleeping by night sleep, and the [ones] getting drunk by night are drunk;

en.L: For those who sleep sleep at night, and those who get drunk are drunk at night.
en.B: Sleepers sleep at night, and drinkers get drunk at night.
en.R: People sleep at night, and people get drunk at night.

decisions.choice: sleep and drunkenness belong to the night
decisions.reason: A plain observation from daily life, used as a picture: those who belong to the day do not live like people of the night.

source.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἡμέρας ὄντες νήφωμεν, ἐνδυσάμενοι θώρακα πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ περικεφαλαίαν ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας·

records.literal_gloss: We but of day being let us be sober, having put on [the] breastplate of faith and love and [as] helmet [the] hope of salvation;

en.L: But since we are of [the] day, let us be sober, having put on [the] breastplate of faith and love, and [as a] helmet [the] hope of salvation.
en.B: But we belong to the day, so let us keep our heads clear, with faith and love for our breastplate and the hope of salvation for our helmet.
en.R: But we belong to the day, so we must keep our minds clear. Our faith and love will protect us like a soldier's armor. Our hope that God will save us will protect us like a helmet.

decisions.choice: breastplate and helmet: God's own armor
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 59:17 God puts on righteousness as a breastplate and salvation as a helmet. Paul gives that armor to believers, as in Ephesians 6:14-17.

decisions.choice: faith, love and hope again
decisions.reason: The three of 1:3 return as armor for the night watch.

decisions.choice: the hope of salvation: confident expectation of final salvation
decisions.reason: σωτηρίας is the rescue at the Lord's coming (verse 9; 1:10). The hope is what guards the mind, as a helmet guards the head.

decisions.choice: like a soldier's armor; Our hope that God will save us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the armor and what the hope is (m1, m3).

source.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἔθετο ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ εἰς περιποίησιν σωτηρίας διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ ἀποθανόντος περὶ ἡμῶν ἵνα εἴτε γρηγορῶμεν εἴτε καθεύδωμεν ἅμα σὺν αὐτῷ ζήσωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: because not appointed us the God for wrath but for obtaining of salvation through the Lord of us Jesus Christ, \v 10 the [one] having died for us, so that whether we are awake or we sleep, together with him we may live.

en.L: For God did not appoint us to wrath but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 10 who died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: For God did not destine us for wrath. He destined us to gain salvation through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, \v 10 who died for us so that, awake or asleep, we may live with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} together.
en.R: God did not choose us to be punished by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. He chose us to be saved through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 10 Jesus died for us, so that we will live together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whether we are still alive when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes or have already died.

decisions.choice: appointed: set us for, destined us to
decisions.reason: τίθημι means to place or appoint. God's purpose for them is salvation, not the wrath of 1:10.

decisions.choice: obtain salvation: come into possession of it
decisions.reason: περιποίησιν means gaining or acquiring: salvation is received through Christ, not earned.

decisions.choice: awake or asleep: alive or dead when the Lord comes
decisions.reason: The verbs are those of verse 6, but here they most likely mean living or having died, which takes up the question of 4:13-18: either way believers will live with Christ.

decisions.choice: who died for us
decisions.reason: περὶ ("for, on behalf of") makes Christ's death the ground of their hope: he died so that they may live (Romans 5:8).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: whether we are still alive when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes or have already died
alternatives: whether we are awake or asleep
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m3.

source.text: διὸ παρακαλεῖτε ἀλλήλους καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε εἷς τὸν ἕνα, καθὼς καὶ ποιεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore encourage one another and build up one the one, just as also you are doing.

en.L: Therefore encourage one another and build one another up, just as you are also doing.
en.B: So keep on encouraging one another and strengthening each other, as you are already doing.
en.R: So encourage each other and help each other grow strong in faith, as you are already doing.

decisions.choice: build up: strengthen, like a building going up
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομέω is the word for building. Believers build up one another's faith (1 Corinthians 14:3-5).

decisions.choice: help each other grow strong in faith
decisions.reason: Readable says what building up means (m1).

source.text: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, εἰδέναι τοὺς κοπιῶντας ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ προϊσταμένους ὑμῶν ἐν κυρίῳ καὶ νουθετοῦντας ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἡγεῖσθαι αὐτοὺς ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ διὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: We ask but you, brothers, to know those laboring among you and leading you in [the] Lord and admonishing you, \v 13 and to regard them beyond all measure in love because of the work of them.

en.L: But we ask you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, to acknowledge those who labor among you and lead you in [the] Lord and admonish you, \v 13 and to regard them most highly in love because of their work.
en.B: We ask you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, to recognize those who work hard among you, who lead you in the Lord and correct you. \v 13 Think of them with the highest respect and love because of the work they do.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we ask you to respect the people who work hard among you. They lead you as people who belong to the Lord, and they warn you when you do wrong. \v 13 Love them and honor them very much because of the work they do.

decisions.choice: acknowledge: recognize and value
decisions.reason: οἶδα, usually "know", here means to recognize someone for who they are and to respect them.

decisions.choice: those who labor, lead and admonish: the church's leaders, described by what they do
decisions.reason: No titles are used. They work hard (κοπιῶντας), lead or care for the church (προϊσταμένους, which can mean both), and correct when needed (νουθετοῦντας, as in Colossians 1:28).

decisions.choice: most highly: beyond all measure
decisions.reason: ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ is the strong word of 3:10.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

source.text: εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Be at peace among yourselves.

en.L: Be at peace among yourselves.
en.B: Keep peace among yourselves.
en.R: Live in peace with each other.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "among yourselves"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "with them", making it a command to live at peace with the leaders just named. The SBLGNT has "among yourselves".

source.text: παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, νουθετεῖτε τοὺς ἀτάκτους, παραμυθεῖσθε τοὺς ὀλιγοψύχους, ἀντέχεσθε τῶν ἀσθενῶν, μακροθυμεῖτε πρὸς πάντας.

records.literal_gloss: We urge now you, brothers, admonish the disorderly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient toward all.

en.L: And we urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}: admonish the disorderly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with everyone.
en.B: We urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}: correct those who are out of line, encourage the fainthearted, stand by the weak, and be patient with everyone.
en.R: We encourage you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, to warn people who are not living as they should. Encourage those who are afraid. Help those who are weak. Be patient with everyone.

decisions.choice: the disorderly: those who are out of line
alternatives: the idle: those who will not work
decisions.reason: ἀτάκτους was used of soldiers out of rank and, in everyday papers of the time, of failing to turn up for work. In view of 4:11 and 2 Thessalonians 3:6-12, it may mean believers who had stopped working; it also covers any who would not live in order.

decisions.choice: the fainthearted and the weak
decisions.reason: ὀλιγοψύχους is the timid or discouraged (perhaps those grieving, 4:13); ἀσθενῶν may be weak in faith or in body.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

source.text: ὁρᾶτε μή τις κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ τινι ἀποδῷ, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε τὸ ἀγαθὸν διώκετε εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας.

records.literal_gloss: See that not anyone evil for evil to anyone repays, but always the good pursue toward one another and toward all.

en.L: See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good for one another and for all.
en.B: See that no one pays back harm with harm. Always go after what is good, for one another and for all people.
en.R: Make sure that no one pays back evil for evil. Always try to do good to each other and to everyone.

decisions.choice: not repaying evil for evil: the teaching of Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus taught his followers not to take revenge (Matthew 5:39-44); Paul says the same in Romans 12:17. In a persecuted church (2:14) the command to do good "to all" includes their opponents.

source.text: πάντοτε χαίρετε, ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε, ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε· τοῦτο γὰρ θέλημα θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Always rejoice, \v 17 unceasingly pray, \v 18 in everything give thanks; this for [is the] will of God in Christ Jesus for you.

en.L: Rejoice always, \v 17 pray unceasingly, \v 18 give thanks in everything; for this is [the] will of God in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus for you.
en.B: Be joyful at all times. \v 17 Never stop praying. \v 18 Whatever happens, give thanks; this is what God wants for you in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: Always be joyful. \v 17 Never stop praying. \v 18 Thank God in every situation. This is what God wants for you who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

decisions.choice: in everything: in every circumstance, not for everything
decisions.reason: ἐν παντὶ means in every situation: believers give thanks in the middle of trouble, not necessarily for the trouble itself.

decisions.choice: this is God's will: for all three commands together
decisions.reason: τοῦτο covers rejoicing, praying and giving thanks: this is what God wants of his people in Christ.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

source.text: τὸ πνεῦμα μὴ σβέννυτε, προφητείας μὴ ἐξουθενεῖτε·

records.literal_gloss: The Spirit not quench, \v 20 prophecies not despise;

en.L: Do not quench the Spirit; \v 20 do not despise prophecies.
en.B: Do not smother the Spirit; \v 20 do not look down on prophecy.
en.R: Do not stop the Holy Spirit from working among you. \v 20 Do not think that messages God gives through people are worthless.

decisions.choice: quench: put out, like a fire
decisions.reason: σβέννυμι is used of putting out a fire or a lamp. The Spirit is pictured as fire (Acts 2:3); believers can stifle what the Spirit is doing among them.

decisions.choice: prophecies: messages given by the Spirit through members of the church
decisions.reason: προφητείας here means words spoken in the church under the Spirit's prompting (1 Corinthians 14:1-5, 14:29-33). Some in Thessalonica may have come to distrust them; verse 21 asks them to test, not to reject.

decisions.choice: Do not stop the Holy Spirit from working among you; messages God gives through people
alternatives: Do not quench the Spirit; prophecies
decisions.reason: Readable says what quenching the Spirit and prophecies are (m1, m2).

source.text: πάντα δὲ δοκιμάζετε, τὸ καλὸν κατέχετε, ἀπὸ παντὸς εἴδους πονηροῦ ἀπέχεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: All [things] but test, the good hold fast, \v 22 from every form of evil abstain.

en.L: But test everything; hold fast to what is good; \v 22 abstain from every form of evil.
en.B: Test everything; keep hold of what is good; \v 22 stay away from evil in every form.
en.R: But test everything to see if it is true. Keep what is good. \v 22 Stay away from every kind of evil.

decisions.choice: test everything: especially prophecies
decisions.reason: δὲ ("but") ties the testing to verse 20: prophecy is not to be despised, but weighed (1 Corinthians 14:29; 1 John 4:1). δοκιμάζω is the word for testing metal.

decisions.choice: every form of evil: evil of any kind
alternatives: every appearance of evil: anything that looks bad
decisions.reason: εἴδους means form or kind. The command is to keep from evil in whatever shape it comes, not merely from what might look wrong to others.

decisions.choice: test everything to see if it is true
decisions.reason: Readable says what testing is for (m1).

source.text: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς ὁλοτελεῖς, καὶ ὁλόκληρον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ τὸ σῶμα ἀμέμπτως ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τηρηθείη.

records.literal_gloss: Himself now the God of the peace may sanctify you wholly, and entire your the spirit and the soul and the body blamelessly at the coming of the Lord of us Jesus Christ may be kept.

en.L: Now may the God of peace {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: May the God of peace {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} make you holy in every part, and may your spirit, soul and body be kept whole and blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: We pray that God, who gives us peace, will make you holy in every way. We pray that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep all of you, your spirit, your soul and your body, without fault until our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} comes back.

decisions.choice: the God of peace: the God who gives peace and wholeness
decisions.reason: Peace here is the wholeness God gives, as in the Hebrew shalom (Romans 15:33).

decisions.choice: completely, entire: every part of you, and nothing missing
decisions.reason: ὁλοτελεῖς means complete through and through; ὁλόκληρον whole, with no part lacking. Both stress the whole person.

decisions.choice: spirit, soul and body: the whole person
alternatives: three separate parts of human nature
decisions.reason: Paul lists the parts to say "all of you", not to give a technical account of human nature. Elsewhere he speaks of body and spirit (1 Corinthians 7:34).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God, who gives us peace
decisions.reason: Readable says what "God of peace" means (m1).

source.text: πιστὸς ὁ καλῶν ὑμᾶς, ὃς καὶ ποιήσει.

records.literal_gloss: Faithful [is] the [one] calling you, who also will do [it].

en.L: Faithful [is] the one who calls you, who will also do [it].
en.B: The God who calls you can be trusted, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it.
en.R: God, who calls you, is faithful. He will do these things for you.

decisions.choice: the one who calls you: God, who goes on calling
decisions.reason: The present καλῶν describes God as the one who calls (2:12). What he has begun he will complete (Philippians 1:6).

decisions.choice: The God who calls you (B); God, who calls you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God (m1).

source.text: Ἀδελφοί, προσεύχεσθε περὶ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Brothers, pray for us.

en.L: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, pray for us.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, pray for us.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, pray for us.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "pray for us"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "also": as Paul prays for them, they should pray for him.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

source.text: ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς πάντας ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Greet the brothers all with a kiss holy.

en.L: Greet all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} with a holy kiss.
en.B: Greet all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} with a holy kiss.
en.R: Greet all the believers with a kiss, as God's family does.

decisions.choice: a holy kiss: the greeting of family
decisions.reason: A kiss was a greeting among relatives and close friends. Believers greeted one another this way as members of one family, and called it "holy" (Romans 16:16; 1 Corinthians 16:20).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: with a kiss, as God's family does
decisions.reason: Readable explains the greeting (m1).

source.text: ἐνορκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν κύριον ἀναγνωσθῆναι τὴν ἐπιστολὴν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: I adjure you [by] the Lord to be read the letter to all the brothers.

en.L: I solemnly charge you [by] the Lord [that] the letter be read to all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: By the Lord, I solemnly charge you: have this letter read to all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: I order you, in the name of the Lord: read this letter to all the believers.

decisions.choice: I solemnly charge you by the Lord: an oath
decisions.reason: ἐνορκίζω is to put someone under oath. The singular "I" is Paul himself, perhaps taking the pen for the end of the letter.

decisions.choice: read to all: read aloud to the whole church
decisions.reason: Letters were read aloud in the assembly (Colossians 4:16). Paul wants every member to hear it, perhaps including those who were not keeping in step (verse 14).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "to all the brothers"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "holy". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: I order you, in the name of the Lord
alternatives: I adjure you by the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable puts the oath in plain words (m1).

source.text: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The grace of the Lord of us Jesus Christ [be] with you.

en.L: The grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [be] with you.
en.B: May the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be with you.
en.R: May the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be with you.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.
